key_insight: Glioma methylation patterns differ by population, and East Asian CGGA glioblastomas showed a distinct epigenetic profile with four methylation-driven genes, including a novel candidate, GLDN.
clinical_relevance: These findings may help refine glioma subtyping and support more population-aware biomarker development for prognosis and personalized treatment strategies.
method: Reclassified glioma samples using WHO 2021 CNS tumour criteria.
Integrated DNA methylation and transcriptomics from CGGA and TCGA.
Applied machine learning classification, clustering, and survival analysis to compare ethnic cohorts.
evidence_signal: In the CGGA cohort, 36.7% of glioblastomas were classified as high-grade astrocytomas by the model, and survival was significantly better than in the non-Hispanic White TCGA glioblastoma cohort (p = 0.037).
watch_item: The study is retrospective and cohort-specific, so the biomarkers and classification performance need external validation before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Methylation-driven Cancer Genes and Methylation Profiling in Glioma: A Comparative Study between East Asian and non-Hispanic White Populations
